themes.corpus_position: Body odor is not just due to sweating but actually the growth of your skin bacteria in the sweat. … First, reduce odor-causing bacteria on the skin by washing well with an anti-bacterial soap, like benzoyl peroxide, also known as PanOxyl, or Hibiclens, which is chlorhexidine. After showering, you can reduce the proliferation of these odor-causing bacteria by applying something that restores the acidity of the skin. This could be glycolic acid, it could be salicylic acid … and use a topical antiperspirant at night. Yes, you heard that right. news.headline: Broadcaster Julie Stewart-Binks: a 'pimple' on her nose was skin cancer
news.summary: Revealed Oct 7 on X: the hockey broadcaster had squamous cell carcinoma on her nose — she thought it was a pimple that wouldn't go away. news.headline: FDA approves first treatment for 'skin writing' hives (symptomatic dermographism)
news.summary: Announced Oct 7: Novartis's oral pill Rhapsido (remibrutinib) is the first FDA-approved treatment for adults whose symptomatic dermographism — hives and itch raised by everyday friction, scratching or rubbing — isn't controlled by antihistamines. In the phase 3 RemIND trial 29.3% were completely hive-free at week 12 versus 14.0% on placebo, with responses as early as week 2.
